prior_value: cheap talk transmits partial information via partition equilibria
observed_value: 0.0pp effect of cheap talk on deal rate; agents produce rapport not value signals
evidence_note: LLM agents do not partition-signal; free-form talk is generic rapport (evidence_trace row 1)

prior_value: smaller b (narrow gap) → finer partitions → more informative talk
observed_value: -10.6pp narrow effect vs -5.0pp wide effect; interaction n.s. (Wald p=0.480)
evidence_note: Communication does not differentially help narrow-gap conditions (evidence_trace row 2)

prior_value: more similar preferences → more informative signaling → higher deal rate
evidence_note: Value gap has massive effect on deals but the channel is feasibility not communication informativeness (evidence_trace row 3)

prior_value: as b→∞ only uninformative equilibrium remains
observed_value: wide gap: 45.6% deal rate vs narrow 76.7%; wide-gap infeasibility rate ~50%
evidence_note: Wide gap produces ~50% infeasible trades as predicted; only uninformative equilibrium observed (evidence_trace row 4)

prior_value: one-sided info maps to pure sender-receiver game; talk should help more
observed_value: -8.3pp interaction (one-sided talk effect worse than two-sided); n.s.
evidence_note: One-sided info does not amplify talk benefit because there is no talk benefit (evidence_trace row 5)

prior_value: costless non-binding communication should weakly improve outcomes
observed_value: 0.0pp for 1-round cheap talk; -23.3pp for extended talk (p=0.004)
evidence_note: Cheap talk is exactly null; extended talk is significantly harmful (evidence_trace row 6)

prior_value: talk more effective when interests more aligned
observed_value: narrow (more aligned): -10.6pp effect; wide (less aligned): -5.0pp effect
evidence_note: Talk effect is slightly more negative when interests are more aligned (evidence_trace row 7)

prior_value: more communication rounds allow finer partitioning
observed_value: extended talk 40.0% vs none 63.3% (p=0.004); actively harmful
evidence_note: More rounds produce more messages but worse outcomes; anchoring dominates partitioning (evidence_trace row 8)

prior_value: separating equilibrium: receiver learns sender type
observed_value: no evidence of value signal transmission in communication messages
evidence_note: Agents do not separate; all communication is pooling/generic rapport (evidence_trace row 9)

prior_value: mutual discipline from multiple audiences improves truthfulness
observed_value: not directly testable in bilateral setting; no truth-telling observed
evidence_note: Bilateral design has single audience; mutual discipline mechanism not applicable (evidence_trace row 10)

prior_value: pooling equilibrium always exists; talk may be uninformative
observed_value: all communication is generic rapport-building; no value signals extracted
evidence_note: LLM agents play the pooling equilibrium universally as predicted (evidence_trace row 11)

prior_value: neologism-proofness favors separating when it exists
observed_value: no separating behavior observed despite favorable conditions (narrow gap + one-sided info)
evidence_note: LLM agents do not respond to neologism-proofness incentives (evidence_trace row 12)

observed_value: +25.8pp (p<0.0001); second largest effect after value gap
evidence_note: Information structure is the dominant treatment effect; not a prior-paper prediction but a key empirical finding

prior_value: no prior prediction for extended talk harm
evidence_note: Extended communication actively hinders bargaining; novel finding not predicted by any theory
